issues.failure_explanation: In the discrete Laplacian the neighbour coefficients are +1/h^2, so the off-diagonal entries of the system matrix are positive and the diagonal is negative. The claim that they are all negative is false, and so is the L_0-type description built on it. The argument offered for stability and O(h^2) convergence of the Euclidean scheme therefore relies on an incorrect property. The cited external argument is also stated for the bounded Dirichlet problem, not for the R^2 problem posed in the same paragraph.

failure_location.quote: the off-diagonal elements of the discrete matrix associated with the discrete FDM system~\eqref{eq:FDM} are all negative

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the correct sign pattern (positive off-diagonals, negative diagonal, zero row sums on the interior), or replace the sentence by the energy/dissipativity argument used later. Restrict the claim to the bounded Dirichlet problem.
issues.overall_effect: The preliminary claim that the Euclidean FDM scheme is stable and converges with order at least O(h^2) is unsupported as written. It is only motivational and does not feed any labelled theorem.
issues.title: Euclidean FDM stability argument rests on a false sign claim for the off-diagonal entries
issues.why_classification: It is a local correction in an illustrative preliminary paragraph and affects none of the main results.

issues.failure_explanation: For the second grid the nodes are (i rho(h), e^{jh}) with j in Z, and H^2_D = [-D,D]x[1/D,D] contains the strip 1/D<=x_2<1 (j<0). The restricted space, however, is defined with Z_2 = {1,...,M}, so only x_2>=e^h is covered. With the zero convention, the row j=1 uses v_{i,0}=0 where the true neighbour is the interior node x_2=1, and the whole strip x_2<1 is dropped. This produces O(1) consistency error and truncation error that the tail control (which only handles the complement of H^2_D) does not absorb. The remark also contradicts the Algorithm, which uses all j with xi_{i,j} in H^2_D, and the node counts in the tables, which correspond to roughly 2M+1 rows.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine Z_2 = {-M',...,M} with M' = floor(log D / h) so the grid covers [1/D,D] consistently with the algorithm, and recheck the zero Dirichlet boundary convention and tail terms at both ends.
issues.overall_effect: The consistency estimate for Delta^(2)_{h,D} as defined is not established, and the convergence statement for the second Laplacian is not supported for the scheme as defined. The numerics appear to use a different (full-range) index set from the one analysed.
issues.title: Truncated second grid omits the part of H^2_D with x_2<1, so the claimed O(h^2) consistency fails
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained redefinition of the index set plus a recheck of the boundary tail estimate, and the result and rate remain comparable.

issues.failure_explanation: With a repeat-until-(k tau > T) loop the update is executed floor(T/tau)+1 times, so the output approximates u at time (floor(T/tau)+1)tau > T. Even when T is a multiple of tau it is u(T+tau), which differs from u(T) by order tau. The theorem, however, analyses exactly k_{tau,T}=floor(T/tau) steps and compares with Pi_h u(T), and claims O(h^2+tau^2) for Crank-Nicolson, so the stated guarantee does not apply to the algorithm as written. Separately, the explicit part (id+tau(1-theta)) lacks the operator Delta_h, which the proof's error recursion presupposes.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the stopping rule to run exactly floor(T/tau) steps (or add a final partial step) and write (id+tau(1-theta)Delta_h) in the update.
issues.overall_effect: The output contract of the algorithm (U approximating u(T) with the stated order) is not met by the pseudocode, and the O(tau^2) claim for theta=1/2 would fail for the output as written.
issues.title: Algorithm stops one step past T and omits Delta_h in the explicit part, contradicting the analysed scheme
issues.why_classification: The fix is a one-line change to the loop condition and the update formula, and the theorem and its proof stand unchanged.
